subject: Regional clearance for SoraTech testimonial — Italian & Korean versions
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Cho <emma.cho@soratech.co.kr>, Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@soratech.it>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Request: permission + regional translations for SoraTech testimonial

Hi Emma / Marco —

Thanks again for the great conversation last week. The customer story we discussed would be a high-impact reference for our EMEA and APAC GTM — we'd like to publish a short testimonial quoting Marco about performance gains and a one-paragraph case summary.

Two asks to make this live:
1) Permission to use Marco's quote and the one-paragraph summary on our website and in a PDF case study.
2) Confirmation that we can publish localized versions in Italian and Korean. We went ahead and drafted the testimonial in English and worked with a translator to produce proposed Italian and Korean copies — attached as v1 drafts. Please treat those as draft translations only.

Attachments: 20260720-soratech-testimonial-draft.docx; soratech-it-translation_v1.docx; soratech-kr-translation_v1.docx

If the translations look OK to you, could you also point me to whoever on your side handles legal/comms sign-off (for Korea and Italy)? If helpful, we can route the copy through our regional legal contacts as well. Ideal timeline: publish lightweight web testimonial + localized PDF by July 30.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-minute call if you'd prefer to talk through wording.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
email: aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com
phone: +1 415 555 0134

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 21:02:00 +09:00
Subject: Re: Request: permission + regional translations for SoraTech testimonial

Hi Aisha —

Thank you — Marco is happy to provide a short quote. I reviewed the English draft and the Korean translation looks ok from a product phrasing standpoint, but I need to run both translations through our internal communications team here in Seoul and our legal/procurement contact to confirm we can post. For Italy, Marco said he'll route the Italian draft to our Milan office and get back to you.

A couple of notes from our side:
- Please confirm whether the testimonial will include any performance numbers (QPS, cost delta). If so, procurement/legal will want to see the source metrics and a short methodology note.
- For Korea, we typically ask for a short local consent form (simple checkbox) prior to publishing — can Redwood provide a DocuSign link we can approve?

Target: we can give final approval by July 29 if there are no heavy legal redlines. I'll copy the right people once I hear back from Milan.

Regards,
Emma
Emma Cho
Head of Customer Marketing, SoraTech
emma.cho@soratech.co.kr

Forwarding thread from Emma at SoraTech — they confirmed Marco is willing but need regional sign-off (Milan + Seoul). They asked about any published performance numbers and requested a DocuSign consent flow for Korea.

Can legal/marketing take a quick look at the attached translations and the draft testimonial (attached) and advise:
- Are there any GDPR/ITA-specific phrasing items we should change in the Italian copy?
- For Korea, is a short consent checkbox + DocuSign link sufficient to meet their typical requirements?
- If we include a single performance metric (latency reduction %), what documentation do we need to attach to the publication?

Attachments copied from original: 20260720-soratech-testimonial-draft.docx; soratech-it-translation_v1.docx; soratech-kr-translation_v1.docx

Thanks — aiming to keep this lightweight; if there are legal concerns we can postpone localization and publish the English version first.

Best,
Aisha

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: permission + regional translations for SoraTech testimonial

Thanks for the flag Aisha — quick legal/marketing notes after a first pass of the drafts:

1) Italian copy: watch the wording around personal data and consent. "We used SoraTech logs" style phrasing can be misread under Italian privacy norms. Suggest replacing with: "Based on our collaboration and anonymized telemetry" — I left a suggestion in the attached IT draft (see soratech-it-translation_v1.docx).

2) Korean consent flow: DocuSign is fine. We should add a single-sentence consent statement in Korean that notes: purpose (marketing testimonial), storage duration (linked to our retention policy), and contact for removal requests. Laura — can you confirm the standard retention line we use for APAC testimonials?

3) Performance metrics: if they want numeric claims (e.g., "30% latency reduction"), we need a one-paragraph methodology + link to the internal eval we ran. Marcus — can you pull the test report we referenced in the POC (runbook and metrics)? I'll include that as an appendix to any published claim.

If Milan/legal push back on anything, we can publish English immediately and roll regional versions after sign-off.

-Vivek
Legal Counsel (on-call) | Redwood Inference

3) Italian edits: Markus and Vivek's suggested wording will be applied to the Italian file; Marco, please review the edit I attached (soratech-it-translation_v1.docx) and let us know if you'd like further changes.
